assessments.reasoning: Eclipse's 2.0 section 1 at [2452,2663) limits the defined category to GNU GPL version 2.0 or a later version, including exceptions or additional permissions identified by the initial Contributor. Naming an unrelated license in a completed form cannot bring it within that definition.

At [6400,6923), section 3.2(a) joins the qualifying separate-file combination and the initial Contributor's notice as conditions for the source-distribution option. Removing either defeats this route. Paragraph (b) adds an independent agreement-copy duty, so satisfying it cannot supply a missing condition in (a).

Exhibit A at [13431,14198) calls for identification of the license or licenses, versions, and applicable exceptions or additional permissions. It expressly rejects the copied-exhibit case and allows a discoverable alternative location. Its placement flexibility supplies no exception to the initial-Contributor or combination requirements in section 3.2(a).

challenge.method: Compared a qualifying separate-file combination and completed initial-Contributor notice with three cases changing one condition at a time: the printed blank exhibit, a completed notice added solely by a downstream party, and a completed initial-Contributor notice without a qualifying combination. Also tested naming a license outside the section 1 definition.
challenge.results: The qualifying combination with the initial Contributor's completed notice permits the option for the identified Secondary License. The blank exhibit fails to select terms. A downstream-only notice fails the actor requirement. A completed notice alone leaves the combination requirement unmet. Naming an unrelated license fails the definition even if both procedural steps are followed.

limitations: Section 2(e) limits the effect of receipt under a Secondary License on additional Contributor grants. Section 3.2(b) separately requires an Agreement copy with each copy of the Program distributed as Source Code.

No individual project's notice, authorship, covered files, combination or selected license was established. Exhibit A permits a location where recipients would look when putting the notice in a particular file is impractical or undesirable.
reasoning: Section 1 defines the eligible Secondary Licenses. For distribution of the Program as Source Code, section 3.2(a) permits availability under such a license when the Program is combined with other material in separate files available under that license and the initial Contributor attached the Exhibit A notice to the Source Code. Exhibit A specifies what the notice must identify and expressly rules out relying on the blank form included in the Agreement. Together these provisions support an optional route with two cumulative conditions.
